text:
The Islanders found out on Friday that they will spend the rest of the season without Kyle Palmieri. The team announced a torn ACL and meniscus in his right knee, six to eight months, and it is the second straight year his season has ended this way. Matthew Schaefer summed it up in a line Stefen Rosner posted: "It's not fair." Palmieri had eight points in 23 games, but his value was always more than the line: a veteran on a young team that has been winning more than its chances say it should.

That gap is the Islanders' season so far. They are +7 in goal difference while the expected goals (the quality of the chances on both sides) have them at -7.4. Goaltending, 13.1 goals saved above expected, is doing the lifting. Tonight it falls to Semyon Varlamov, starting over Ilya Sorokin, who has 17 of the 24 starts. Varlamov has been sharp in a small sample: +5.1 in seven games. Up front, Pete DeBoer has put Mathew Barzal back with Bo Horvat and Simon Holmstrom, and both centres have been near 25 minutes a night since Palmieri went down.

Winnipeg comes in 3-1-1 in its last five after a 4-2 win in Boston, with Kyle Connor and Mark Scheifele carrying the attack. Scheifele has 19 points in his last ten and set the franchise goals record last weekend; Connor has nine points in a four-game streak. The Jets are without Dylan DeMelo and Vladislav Namestnikov, and Stuart Skinner starts in net (+2.2 this season), a day before Connor Hellebuyck faces his old team for the first time since the trade.

The last meeting, Nov. 19 in Winnipeg, went to overtime and the Jets took it 4-3, a game they deserved 62% of the time. Our numbers have this one close: 3.06 expected goals for Winnipeg, 3.17 for the Islanders. Logan Stanley gets his first look at the Jets after 261 games in their colours, and Alex Iafallo sits one point from 300.
headline: Islanders lose Palmieri again, and turn to Varlamov
